stories.title: Actin conformation dynamics precede force generation in cytotoxic T lymphocytes
stories.description: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) are cells of the adaptive immune system that are able to recognise and kill cancerous or virally infected target cells. The biochemical basis of CTL-mediated killing has been examined in great detail. Recent work has underscored the importance of physical forces in T cell function too, but how CTLs sense and exert force during migration and killing is not fully understood. Here, by expressing actin conformation probes based on the CH domain of utrophin, we directly visualize regions of altered F-actin conformation in primary CTLs during migration and killing. By combining these probes with traction force microscopy, we correlate external force with the internal cytoskeleton. We show that actin conformation is regulated upstream of force production, and that force exertion at the cytotoxic immune synapse temporally follows actin conformation dynamics. Our work offers insight into the relationship between cellular force production and F-actin conformation in important primary immune cells.

stories.title: Environmental surveillance of antimicrobial resistance: the missing pillar in Europe’s One Health strategy
stories.description: The presence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants in the environment enables their dissemination and transfer from and into human microbiomes. Environmental surveillance is a recognized cornerstone for evaluating, understanding, and mitigating emergence and exposure to resistant pathogens. However, despite its growing recognition within European One Health frameworks, environmental surveillance has not yet evolved into a systematic, transmission-oriented approach capable of elucidating pathways of transfer to human pathogens or identifying critical intervention nodes. While human and animal surveillance systems are increasingly harmonized across Europe, environmental AMR data remains fragmented, gathered in a methodologically inconsistent manner, and consequently often treated as unimportant. We argue that environmental surveillance must become a sustained component of Europe’s AMR response, within an effective One Health-based control strategy. Drawing on data collected through a structured comparative policy analysis of 18 national plans against AMR, covering more than 76% of the European population, as well as recent EU-level initiatives (e.g., Eionet pilot study, JAMRAI2, EU-WISH, the European Partnership on One Health Antimicrobial Resistance EUP OHAMR, and the EU Directives 2024/3019, 2026/809), we conclude that despite a common recognition of the importance of the issue and an apparent willingness to evolve, initiatives vary in their focus, resource allocation, methodological approaches, and governance structures. The vast body of gray literature and long-term environmental data that remain underused could contribute to the foundations of harmonization across sectors and international data integration and sharing. Environmental AMR surveillance is an urgent societal, regulatory, and scientific imperative.

stories.title: Limited impact of the 2025 Kamchatka tsunami explained by the complex seismic rupture
stories.description: The great 29th of July 2025 megathrust earthquake of magnitude 8.8, which occurred near the Kamchatka Peninsula, Russia, generated a local tsunami comparable to that of its larger 1952 predecessor, which, in contrast, caused a larger tsunami along the far-field Pacific shorelines. The 2025 tsunami was also smaller than anticipated by the life-saving tsunami warning issued for the far-field Pacific shorelines. By jointly inverting SWOT and DART tsunami data, InSAR and GNSS data, here we show that the 2025 earthquake rupture occurred within or adjacent to the 1952 source area, with an uncertain degree of overlap. We also show that a smaller tsunami potential energy due to earthquake magnitude and relatively deep slip explains the moderate far-field impact. Conversely, some shallow displacement that reaches the trench explains the enhanced local runup, comparable to the 1952 runup, despite the smaller magnitude of the 2025 earthquake. Our findings are supported by comparisons with previous tsunamis (2010 Maule, Chile, and 2005 Nias, Indonesia). A joint inversion of sea-surface and satellite data suggests the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake exhibited only limited shallow slip and seafloor deformation which explains the suppressed far-field amplitudes despite substantial local run-up.

stories.title: Temperature and trap charge sensitivity analysis of a Si-Ge heterojunction dual stack source raised drain tunnel FET
stories.description: This work investigates the impact of interface trap charges (ITCs) and temperature on the DC and RF/analog performance of a dual-stack source raised-drain tunnel field-effect transistor (DSSRD-TFET). The device uses a silicon–germanium source stack and raised-drain architecture to improve electrostatic control, enhance tunneling efficiency, and suppress leakage. Negative interface trap charges (NITC), zero interface trap charges (ZITC), and positive interface trap charge (PITC) conditions are analyzed using Sentaurus TCAD from 200 to 400 K. PITC increases the ON-state current (IOn) by strengthening the tunneling-junction electric field and enhancing carrier accumulation but simultaneously reducing the subthreshold steepness, leading to a higher subthreshold swing (SS). In contrast, NITC suppresses IOn but provides better subthreshold control, resulting in lower SS. At 300 K, the DSSRD-TFET achieves an IOn of 1.12 × 10–4 A/µm, an OFF-state current (IOff) of 1.55 × 10–18 A/µm, and an IOn/IOff ratio of 7.27 × 1013 under PITC. Temperature-dependent simulations show that PITC maintains the strongest RF/analog response across the studied temperature range.
